contribution.position: I hold my earlier position. I am answering product's claim that nobody else sees a reliability problem, so it can be treated as settled. Other roles not raising it does not settle it. The artifact:cost-sheet that product cites covers budget only (+3% against a 5% ceiling) and says nothing about error rate. artifact:incident-log still shows a 30-day error rate of 2.6% against a 0.5% SLO and two sev2 incidents. I also answer qa's claim that risk is contained. artifact:test-report (412 passed, 0 failed, 87% coverage) is pre-release test evidence. It does not measure live error rate, so it cannot rebut the incident log. One new point: the incident log is titled as being for the pricing refresh, so the breach may be attributable to the refresh path itself rather than the surrounding system. That would make it more serious than I framed it before. The artifact list does not settle this, because no artifact attributes the errors to a specific path. There is also no root-cause or remediation record for the two sev2s, and no artifact shows the refresh would lower or hold the error rate. Until those gaps are filled, reliability is unresolved, not settled. The runbook rollback in artifact:ops-runbook reduces recovery cost but does not address the existing breach.
